title: Minimum Cost to Make Array Equal
summary: Given two 0-indexed arrays, nums and cost, each containing n positive integers, you can perform the following operation any number of times: - Increase or decrease any element in the nums array by 1.
statement: Given two 0-indexed arrays, nums and cost, each containing n positive integers, you can perform the following operation any number of times: - Increase or decrease any element in the nums array by 1. - The cost of performing one operation on the i-th element is given by cost[i]. Determine the minimum total cost required to make all elements in the nums array equal.
constraints: nums and cost are equally sized nonempty arrays of positive integers.
Changing nums[i] by one in either direction costs cost[i].
Return the minimum total cost needed to make all values equal.
hints: The objective is a weighted sum of absolute distances.
Sort values and choose the first value whose cumulative weight reaches half the total weight.
Find the weighted median, then sum abs(value-target)*cost.

Moving the target across a value transfers that weight from the decreasing side to the increasing side; the slope first becomes nonnegative at a weighted median, which therefore minimizes the convex cost.
editorial: Moving the target across a value transfers that weight from the decreasing side to the increasing side; the slope first becomes nonnegative at a weighted median, which therefore minimizes the convex cost.

tests.explanation: Choosing target two costs 2+3+3=8, which is minimal.
Every value is already equal, so the minimum cost is zero.
